text: DeskBox is a free, open-source desktop organizer for Windows 10/11. It adds freely placeable "widgets" to the native desktop: file widgets manage real local files — collect, map, stack, group and organize — keeping the desktop tidy. Six built-in feature widgets (Todo, Quick Capture, Clipboard, Music, Weather, and Glance) keep daily essentials one glance away, alongside Alt+D Global Search (enabled by default) and AI-built Custom Widgets running in an isolated sandbox. It does not replace the Windows desktop or take over File Explorer. Files stay normal files, everything works the way you know, and data stays on your machine by default. Everything works out of the box: the Direct installer is free and open source forever with zero ads or subscriptions; starting in 1.6.0, DeskBox uses a GPL-3.0-only + Commercial dual license with an explicit GPL copyleft exemption for standalone .dbxwidget custom widgets you build or share. What kind of software is DeskBox? A free, open-source desktop organizer for Windows 10/11: it places "widgets" on the native desktop to manage files, built-in widgets, and custom widgets with Global Search — it never replaces the desktop or takes over File Explorer, and you can exit at any time. Does it replace my Windows desktop? No. Windows Explorer remains the desktop shell; DeskBox only adds independently managed widgets on top, and files stay normal files (see "Does DeskBox replace the Windows desktop?"). Is it paid? Any ads or subscriptions? The Direct build is free and open source forever (GPL-3.0-only + Commercial dual license starting in 1.6.0, with standalone .dbxwidget custom widgets exempt from copyleft) — no ads, no subscription. The Microsoft Store build is an optional paid supporter channel. Can I add my own features? Since 1.6.0 you can create native custom widgets with AI in Widget Studio (zero WebView UI + offline QuickJS sandbox), or import .dbxwidget packages shared by others (see "Build your own widgets with AI: Widget Workshop basics").

text: Drag a widget by its title bar to move it; drag the edges or corners to resize. When an edge approaches another widget or the screen edge, snap guide lines appear to help you line things up. The minimum size for regular widgets is 150×150; since 1.5.9, expanded widgets can go as small as 25 DIP, so they tuck away neatly. Sizes and positions are remembered per monitor topology and restored automatically after display changes. Hold Ctrl and drag any widget's title bar to move every widget on that screen as one — no more repositioning them one by one. Right-click a widget title bar → "Widget lock" to enable "Lock position" or "Lock size" (or show those quick buttons under Settings → Windows & interaction → Widget action buttons). Locking only disables manual dragging and resizing: layout restoration, monitor changes, or group reordering can still move the widget. How small can a widget get? Regular widgets bottom out at 150×150; since 1.5.9 expanded widgets can shrink to 25 DIP — update to the latest version to enjoy it. My widget keeps getting dragged away. Can I pin it? Right-click its title bar → "Widget lock" → "Lock position" or "Lock size" (or toggle title-bar lock buttons). Locking only disables dragging and resizing — layout restoration, monitor switches, and group reordering can still move it. How do I move a whole screen of widgets at once? Hold Ctrl and drag any widget's title bar — every widget on the current screen moves as one. Widget positions went wrong after changing monitors. Layouts are remembered per monitor combination, and a new combination gets an automatic layout. Gather things up with "Move all to this display" under Settings → Windows & interaction → Displays (see "Widgets missing or misplaced after restart or monitor changes").

text: The taskbar tray icon is your main control hub: left-click to show or hide all widgets immediately; right-click to access "Organize desktop…", "Global search", "New widget", "New folder mapping", "Add feature widget", "Open storage folder", "Settings", and "Exit" (plus an update item when available). In the Microsoft Store edition, right-clicking the DeskBox taskbar button also provides a Jump List with New widget, New folder mapping, Toggle widgets, Open storage folder, and Settings. DeskBox includes three global hotkeys: (1) Widget show/hide (F7, Double Control, Alt+Space, Win+Space, single Win, Copilot key, Double Shift, Double Space under Settings → Windows & interaction → Global hotkey); (2) Global Search (Alt+D, enabled by default on new installs under Settings → Global search → Search hotkey); and (3) Clipboard Quick-paste (Alt+V under Settings → Feature widgets → Clipboard). Hold keys to record any Win/Ctrl/Alt/Shift + F1–F24 combination; conflicts with other apps are explicitly rejected. Single modifiers and Space become usable via the "Double-tap trigger" checkbox. Claiming Win+Space temporarily overrides Windows input-language switching; claiming the single Win key means opening Start with Ctrl+Esc; claiming Alt+Space overrides the window system menu. Pick another combination anytime if preferred. The tray icon can be set to "Hidden" under Settings → Appearance → App theme → Tray icon. Launching DeskBox again from the Start menu or desktop (or searching Settings via Alt+D) opens Settings directly so the entry point is never lost. F7 doesn't respond. What should I do? Check Settings → Windows & interaction → Global hotkey to verify F7 is still assigned; conflicts with other apps are rejected during recording. Global hotkeys can also fail if DeskBox runs elevated above a standard-privilege foreground window — restart with standard privileges (see "Double-click or hotkey won't bring widgets back up?"). Can I customize the shortcuts? Yes. Record or change combinations in Settings → Windows & interaction (show/hide), Settings → Global search (Search hotkey), and Settings → Feature widgets → Clipboard (Quick-paste popup); conflicts are flagged cleanly. I hid the tray icon. How do I open Settings again? Launch DeskBox again from the Start menu or desktop to open Settings directly, or press Alt+D and search "Tray icon" to change it back under Settings → Appearance → App theme → Tray icon. After taking over the single Win key, how do I open the Start menu? Use Ctrl+Esc. That's the known effect of taking over the single Win key; switch to another hotkey if you'd rather not have it.

text: Collect widgets move dragged files into a real storage folder — best for temporary files piling up on the desktop. Mapped folder widgets simply show an existing folder (a project directory, your downloads) on the desktop without moving anything. Files in both widget types open, copy, rename and delete normally; Explorer sees the exact same files. Default drop behavior is configured uniformly in Settings; hold Alt (or Ctrl+Shift) while dropping to create only a shortcut and leave the original file untouched. Dropping a file with the same name never overwrites; DeskBox creates "File name (2)" instead. Never drag a main .exe or app install folder (such as WeChat or QQ) straight into a collect widget — moving it away from its install directory breaks logins and updates. Drag its desktop .lnk shortcut, or hold Alt while dropping to create a shortcut only. The right-click menu inside widgets includes native conveniences: if double-clicking an elevated installer or admin tool does nothing, right-click and choose "Run as administrator"; other actions include "Open file location", "Copy as path", "Compress to" (ZIP or tar), and "Extract all". Windows 10 drag & drop note: due to WinUI 3 limitations on Windows 10, "Use Windows default" uses a safe compatible drag-out that keeps originals in DeskBox. In "Move" mode, if a browser or external app rejects a drop, drag once more or hold Ctrl at drag start for a one-time compatible drop. Windows 11 offers fuller native drag-and-drop. How do I put a program in a widget without moving it? Hold Alt (or Ctrl+Shift) while dragging the program into the widget — only a shortcut is created and the original stays in its install folder (critical for apps like WeChat so logins don't reset). Will dropping two files with the same name overwrite one? No. Same-named files never overwrite each other; DeskBox automatically creates a new name like "File name (2)". Does a mapped folder widget move my files? No. Mapped widgets only display a folder you choose and move nothing; collect widgets are the ones that move dropped files into the storage folder. Can I zip files directly inside a widget? Yes. Right-click the selection and choose "Compress to" — ZIP or tar; archives also support "Extract all". Nothing happens when I double-click an admin installer or utility shortcut in a widget. Tools requiring UAC elevation may silently fail on double-click from a standard session — right-click the item inside the widget and pick "Run as administrator". Why does dragging out on Windows 10 copy instead of moving? Due to Windows 10 WinUI 3 constraints, "Use Windows default" safely keeps originals when dragging out; switch "File drag & drop behavior" to Move or hold Shift/Ctrl as needed. Default storage path New collect widgets create separate folders here; expand for "Pin to File Explorer Quick Access", "Desktop storage shortcut", and "Unlinked storage folders". File drag & drop behavior Unified 1.6.0 setting controlling drag-in, drag-out, and cross-widget drops; hold Shift to move, Ctrl to copy, Alt to create a shortcut, plus "Modifier key tips" and "Drop result notification". Open items with Under "Opening & context menu": choose single-click or double-click to open files and folders. Folder opening Under "Opening & context menu": browse child folders inside the current widget or open them in File Explorer. Use system context menu Under "Opening & context menu": right-clicking a single file shows the native Windows menu (off by default); stacks and multi-select keep the built-in menu. Windows 10 drag & drop note On Windows 10, "Use Windows default" safely copies out so external drops never delete local originals unexpectedly.

title: Where did my files go? Storage location and moving files back
summary: DeskBox file widgets manage real local files. Dragging files into a collect widget moves them into a DeskBox storage folder; a mapped folder

Does uninstalling DeskBox delete my files?
Why can't WeChat / QQ find the files from my widget when sending?
Can I change the default storage path safely?
I closed a widget and clicked "Move files to desktop", but can't find them on my desktop?
paths: Settings → Files & organization → Default storage path
text: DeskBox file widgets manage real local files. Dragging files into a collect widget moves them into a DeskBox storage folder; a mapped folder widget only displays a folder you choose and never moves anything. Files in both widget types open, copy and delete normally, and Explorer sees the same files — the only difference is that collected files now live in the storage directory instead of their original location. Check Settings → Files & organization → Default storage path for the exact location on your PC (commonly D:\DeskBox, or DeskBox under your user profile; enable "Desktop storage shortcut" or "Pin to File Explorer Quick Access" for instant access, and inspect "Unlinked storage folders" for orphaned folders). That's also where to browse when sending files via WeChat or QQ. Drag files straight from the widget back to the desktop, or right-click → Cut / "Move back to desktop", then paste at the destination. To relocate everything: open the default storage path and move the widget's folder wherever you need it. To change the storage location (1.5.6+ safe migration): upfront checks block Desktop, subfolders, network, or removable drives; then a preview and phased copy run with dual-side hash verification (supporting retry/skip) and never auto-delete originals at the old location. Uninstalling DeskBox never deletes files; when closing a non-empty collect widget, you can choose "Keep files…", "Move files to desktop", or "Also move the widget's folder to the Recycle Bin". If you chose "Move files to desktop" and don't see them, check OneDrive Desktop redirection (C:\Users\<user>\OneDrive\Desktop vs local Desktop), your Default storage path, and the Recycle Bin. Want files to stay where they are and still appear on the desktop? Use a mapped folder widget (see "How do I put an existing folder on the desktop?") — it moves nothing. Why did files disappear from the desktop after I put them in a widget? Collect widgets move files into the storage directory, so the original desktop location is naturally empty. Everything is under the default storage path and can be dragged or moved back at any time. Does uninstalling DeskBox delete my files? No. DeskBox never deletes user files on uninstall, and the storage folder and mapped folders remain intact under the default storage path. Why can't WeChat / QQ find the files from my widget when sending? Files collected from the desktop live in the storage directory. Enable "Pin to File Explorer Quick Access" under Default storage path for one-click browsing, or drag straight from the widget into the chat. Can I change the default storage path safely? Yes — under Settings → Files & organization → Default storage path. DeskBox copies and hash-verifies every item before switching and leaves originals intact; Desktop, nested subfolders, network, and removable paths are rejected to prevent loops. I closed a widget and clicked "Move files to desktop", but can't find them on my desktop? OneDrive Desktop backup redirects Desktop to C:\Users\<user>\OneDrive\Desktop instead of local Desktop. Check both desktop folders, the default storage path, and the Recycle Bin.

text: Choose Tray right-click → "New folder mapping", or click + on a widget title bar → "New folder mapping". Pick the directory you want on the desktop (such as a project folder or Downloads). Its contents appear directly in the widget; removing a mapping only closes the view and deletes none of your files. After entering subfolders inside a mapped widget, right-click for "Go up one level" or "Back to original folder". Each widget can also override "Folder opening" to browse in-widget, open in File Explorer, or follow global defaults. See the "Cannot map this folder" conflict dialog? Starting in 1.6.0, DeskBox names the exact relation (same, inside, contains, or occupied widget): you cannot map a folder inside the "Default storage path" or overlapping another widget. To turn a subfolder currently inside a collect widget into its own mapped widget, move that subfolder outside managed storage in File Explorer first, then map it; external parent and child folders can both be mapped separately. Because Microsoft Store MSIX virtualization exposes AppData as read-only, dropping or editing files inside a mapped AppData folder is blocked in the Store edition; use the Direct installer if you need full write access to AppData. I'm several folders deep in a mapped widget — how do I get back to the start? Right-click the widget and use "Go up one level" to step back, or "Back to original folder" to return to the mapped root in one jump. Does a mapped widget move or copy my files? No. Mapped widgets only display an existing folder on the desktop — every action applies to the original folder itself, and removing the mapping deletes nothing. Can subfolders open in Explorer instead? Yes. Set per-widget folder opening or configure global "Folder opening" under Settings → Files & organization → Opening & context menu. Why does DeskBox show "Cannot map this folder"? The selected directory is either identical to, overlapping with, or located inside DeskBox's "Default storage path" (nested folders inside managed storage are disallowed to avoid dual-widget conflicts). Move that subfolder outside managed storage first, or click the dialog button to jump to the occupying widget.

text: Every file widget can independently switch between icon and list views, with per-widget sorting and spacing (right-click empty space in any widget → "View" or "Sort by"). Since 1.5.9, selecting a file expands its name in place to show the full text; click the name once more (or press F2) to rename it inline — no context menu needed. Prefer the Windows menu? Enable "Use system context menu" under Settings → Files & organization → Opening & context menu. Widgets also support creating folders/files, keyboard Delete (Recycle Bin) / Shift+Delete (permanent) / F2, and ZIP/tar compress & extract (click an item inside the widget first so it holds keyboard focus). Starting in 1.6.0, "Icon size", "Horizontal/Vertical spacing", "File name width/lines", "Show image & video thumbnails", "Show file extensions", and "Hide shortcut arrow overlay" are unified under Settings → Files & organization → File & icon display, while title-bar action buttons moved to Settings → Windows & interaction → Widget action buttons. How do I rename a file inside a widget? Click once to select the file, then click its name again to rename it inline (since 1.5.9), press F2, or choose Rename from the right-click menu. File names are truncated when they're long. What can I do? Selecting a file expands its name in place; "File name width" and "File name lines" are also adjustable under Settings → Files & organization → File & icon display. Can I use the original Windows context menu? Yes. Enable "Use system context menu" under Settings → Files & organization → Opening & context menu to show the native Windows menu on single-file right-clicks; stacks and multi-select keep the built-in menu. Icons and text are too small on a high-resolution screen. "Icon size" and spacing live under Settings → Files & organization → File & icon display, while global "Text size" and "Overall density" live under Settings → Appearance → Display density (see "Text size and icon size"). Why are image thumbnails missing (e.g. network drives / OneDrive), or why don't Delete / arrow keys respond? (1) Thumbnails come from Windows Shell: verify "Show image & video thumbnails" is enabled, noting that mapped network drives, cloud-only OneDrive placeholders, or special formats may fall back to file icons. (2) Click an item inside the widget first to give it keyboard focus before pressing Delete, F2, or arrow keys. Icon size / Horizontal spacing / Vertical spacing Under "File & icon display → Icon size and spacing": adjusts file-widget icon scale and grid density globally (overridable per widget via right-click → View → Icon size). File name lines Hide file names or show them on one or two lines in icon view. File name width Adjust the horizontal width available to file names. Show image & video thumbnails On by default to preview image and video thumbnails; turn off to display Windows file icons only. Show file extensions Display extensions such as .txt and .png in item names. Exclude .lnk shortcuts Keep .lnk app shortcut names clean when "Show file extensions" is enabled. Hide shortcut arrow overlay Applies only to icons inside DeskBox widgets without altering Windows registry settings. List details Show size, modified time, or folder item count in list view. Show path tooltips Show full file paths when hovering items. Use system context menu Under Settings → Files & organization → Opening & context menu: right-clicking a single file shows the native Windows menu (off by default); stacks and multi-select keep the built-in menu.

text: Stacking compresses groups of similar files into expandable stacks, keeping the widget tidy while everything stays reachable. Manual stacks are preserved separately, and stacking never moves your actual files. Automatic stacking: enable "Automatic stacking" under Settings → Files & organization → File stacks (or toggle per-widget "Automatic stacks" from the widget's blank-area right-click menu). Manual stacking: even with automatic stacking off, select multiple regular files and right-click → "Start stacking", or drop a file onto a non-executable tile or existing stack. Click a stack to expand it inline or in a popover panel; right-click a stack to move up/down, expand and select contents, or dissolve. Custom format rules can be reordered by dragging to change priority: rules match top to bottom and each file joins the first rule it hits, with a live "Matched N items" preview as you edit. Dropped a file onto an app shortcut / .exe expecting a stack and the app opened the file instead? Dropping onto an executable opens the file with that app by design — multi-select both icons and right-click → "Start stacking" to stack shortcuts. Does stacking move my files? No. Stacking is a display layer only — manual stacks are preserved separately and actual files never move. How do custom rules decide which stack a file joins? Rules match top to bottom and each file joins the first rule it hits; drag rules to change priority, watching the live "Matched N items" preview as you adjust. I want manual stacking only, no automatic stacks. Turn off "Automatic stacking" under Settings → Files & organization → File stacks — multi-selecting files and choosing "Start stacking" keeps working. How many same-type files trigger an automatic stack? "Files needed to form a stack" decides: a stack forms only after a category reaches the configured count, avoiding fragmentation. Dropping a file onto an icon opened it instead of creating a stack. Dropping onto an .exe or app shortcut opens the file with that app. To stack apps or shortcuts, select multiple tiles and right-click → "Start stacking". text: The music widget does not talk to NetEase Cloud Music, QQ Music or other players directly — it reads the Windows System Media Transport Controls (SMTC). Track info, cover art and playback controls are reported by the player to Windows, and DeskBox reads them from Windows. If a player reports nothing, the widget cannot detect it — that is the root of most "not detected" cases. Start playing a song in your player. Press a volume key and watch the Windows volume flyout. If the flyout shows the player name and track, the pipeline works and DeskBox should detect it; if it shows nothing, the player is not connected to the system media session — turn on the matching switch in the player's own settings. NetEase Cloud Music: the matching switch in its own settings must be on, and player updates often reset it — if detection breaks again after an update, check that switch first. Even with the switch on, NetEase only reports cover art plus next/pause controls; the missing progress bar is a limit of what the player reports. QQ Music integration is more complete, but dragging the progress bar is not supported there either. Browser audio sources work well but take priority over players — when a browser steals the session, use "Switch media source" in the music widget menu to pin control to your player. Since 1.6.0, the music widget supports synced lyrics and real-time Audio spectrum motion: local lyric files match first, falling back to the online LRCLIB library. LRCLIB is a free public catalog, so obscure tracks may lack online lyrics unless you point "Local lyrics folder" at your own files or QQ Music cache. Open Settings → Feature widgets → Music and make sure "Show lyrics" is on. Point "Local lyrics folder" at the folder where your lyrics live. Play a track — DeskBox scrolls synced lyrics line by line; toggle or restyle "Audio spectrum" in Settings or the widget right-click menu. "Local lyrics folder" can point straight at your QQ Music cache root (for example F:\QQMusicCache): DeskBox automatically scans QQMusicLyricNew, QQMusicLyric, Lyric and Lyrics subfolders, recognizes QQ Music naming (±1s tolerance) and KuGou md5 files, or scans Artist/Album folders; 10 formats are supported (.qrc, .yrc, .krc, .lrcx, .lrc, .ttml, .srt, .vtt, NetEase .json/.txt) with automatic translation merge and GB18030 support (up to 2 MB/file, 10,000 files/scan). If lyrics run ahead or lag behind, calibrate on the widget: "0.5 s earlier", "0.5 s later" or "Reset lyrics offset" — offsets save per track. Instrumental tracks show an instrumental notice instead of lyrics. Turn on "Show live lyrics in capsule mode" to keep lyrics while collapsed — the current line appears in the capsule's subtitle slot. NetEase Cloud Music isn't detected and the music widget never shows the track. What should I do? First enable the system media session toggle in NetEase Cloud Music's own settings (updates often reset it), then check whether pressing a volume key displays the track in the Windows volume flyout. If the flyout shows it but the widget still won't, attach a diagnostics bundle from Settings → About → Troubleshooting & diagnostics. Why do some songs have lyrics while others don't? Online lyrics come from LRCLIB — a free public catalog with gaps for rare tracks. Set "Local lyrics folder" under Settings → Feature widgets → Music (you can point straight at QQ Music's cache); local lyrics always take priority. The progress bar is missing or frozen — can that be fixed? It's a player limitation: NetEase Cloud Music does not report track position via Windows SMTC and QQ Music doesn't allow seeking. For NetEase progress reporting, some users evaluate third-party plugin inflink-rs (unofficial — use at your own discretion). The widget shows what's playing in my browser, not my player. Why? Browsers take priority in Windows SMTC. Use "Switch media source" in the music widget menu to pin control to your preferred player. Why doesn't the vinyl record spin? The record is a display mode (vertical or horizontal vinyl). If vinyl mode is selected but stays still, check whether "Vinyl rotation" is disabled under Settings → General → Performance & resources → Continuous decorative effects. Lyrics run half a beat ahead of (or behind) the vocal — adjustable? Yes. Tap "0.5 s earlier" or "0.5 s later" on the music widget, or "Reset lyrics offset"; offsets are remembered per track. text: Blank, blurry, or globe icons inside widgets usually trace back to the icon resource itself, a stale system icon cache, or turning off "Show image & video thumbnails". Run del /a %LOCALAPPDATA%\IconCache.db, then del /a /q %LOCALAPPDATA%\iconcache_*.db %LOCALAPPDATA%\thumbcache_*.db to delete icon and thumbnail caches. Run ie4uinit.exe -show to refresh system icons. Finally use Run new task to start explorer and check the icons back on the desktop. The "Hide shortcut arrow overlay" toggle can also interact with shell icons: if icons turn white while it is enabled, turn it off under Settings → Files & organization → File & icon display and check if they recover. Check hotkey conflicts and privileges: re-record your show/hide key under Settings → Windows & interaction → Global hotkey or Alt+D under Settings → Global search → Search hotkey. If desktop double-click conflicts with Directory Opus, switch to a pure keyboard shortcut like F7; if DeskBox runs elevated above standard windows, choose "Restart with standard privileges" from the tray. Triggered accidentally near taskbar or third-party shell tools? Disable or re-enable "Double-click blank desktop space" under Settings → Windows & interaction → Widget layer anytime. Hold keys to record any Win/Ctrl/Alt/Shift + F1–F24 combo; presets include F7, Double Control, Alt+Space, Win+Space, single Win, Double Shift, and Double Space. Show/hide lag fixed in 1.5.9 is joined in 1.6.0 by focus and IME hardening across wakeups and Global Search. Use the top Settings search bar (Ctrl+F) or Alt+D and type "double-click", "Global hotkey", or "Search hotkey" to jump straight there. Double-clicking the desktop does nothing and widgets won't come up. What now? Left-click the tray icon to toggle immediately; Windows hook drops auto-heal in ~30 seconds or reset by toggling "Double-click blank desktop space" off and on (if it conflicts with Directory Opus, use a pure keyboard hotkey like F7). F7 doesn't respond, or widgets won't rise above windows. On the Desktop pinned layer, F7 intentionally only shows/hides behind apps — use Dynamic layer or Quick reveal to summon over windows. Otherwise re-record the hotkey under Settings → Windows & interaction and ensure standard privileges. Alt+D Global Search hotkey isn't opening search. Check Settings → Global search → Search hotkey to confirm it is enabled (on by default on new installs) and has no app conflict, or click Tray right-click → "Global search". Hotkeys stopped working and switching combinations didn't help. Run Drag-and-drop check & Background service status under Settings → About → Troubleshooting & diagnostics, update to 1.6.0, and attach a diagnostics bundle if it persists. Summoning widgets from hidden state lags. That lag was fixed in 1.5.9; keeping "Keep UI cache while hidden" enabled under Settings → General → Performance & resources makes re-reveals instant.

title: Doesn't start with Windows, or starts slowly
summary: When DeskBox doesn't launch at login or appears slowly, it usually traces back to the startup toggle or a disabled state in Windows Startup
faqs: DeskBox doesn't start with Windows. What should I do?
DeskBox isn't in Task Manager's startup list or shows Disabled.
I have to open it manually every time. Can't it start automatically?
Startup feels slow — widgets only show up a while after login.
My desktop icons got scrambled after autostart.
text: When DeskBox doesn't launch at login or appears slowly, it usually traces back to the startup toggle or a disabled state in Windows Startup Apps. Open Settings → General and make sure "Launch at startup" is toggled on. If already on yet failing: toggle "Launch at startup" off and back on once to clear stale disabled flags; if a status banner card appears below it, click "Open system settings" and verify DeskBox is enabled in Windows Settings → Apps → Startup. On Microsoft Store builds, verify DeskBox in Windows Startup Apps; on Direct builds, reboot once to test after re-registering. For a quiet login: turn on "Silent startup" so DeskBox initializes cleanly in the tray without interrupting until you press F7 or Alt+D. Widgets appearing several seconds after login is normal: Windows initializes the desktop shell first and autostarted apps follow cleanly. Autostart scrambling native desktop icons was resolved in 1.5.9 — stay on the latest release. Migrating from Microsoft Store to Direct? Uninstall the Store edition after Direct imports your data so Windows doesn't launch two separate startup entries. DeskBox doesn't start with Windows. What should I do? Verify "Launch at startup" is on under Settings → General, toggle it off and on to reset registration, and click "Open system settings" if shown to check Windows Startup Apps. DeskBox isn't in Task Manager's startup list or shows Disabled. Toggle "Launch at startup" off and back on under Settings → General, or use "Open system settings" to re-enable it in Windows. I have to open it manually every time. Can't it start automatically? Enable "Launch at startup" plus "Silent startup" under Settings → General so DeskBox waits quietly in the system tray at login. Startup feels slow — widgets only show up a while after login. Windows brings up desktop shell services before user startup apps; a short post-login delay is normal. My desktop icons got scrambled after autostart. Fixed in 1.5.9 — update to the latest release.

title: Update fails or the download is slow
summary: The Direct build's in-app updater downloads installers from GitHub, so poor connectivity causes slow downloads or failures; insufficient pri
faqs: The update fails or won't update — what should I do?
The download is really slow — do I need a proxy?
It's been stuck on "Extracting" forever.
The update says I don't have enough privileges.
Installation says my system version isn't supported.
text: The Direct build's in-app updater downloads installers from GitHub, so poor connectivity causes slow downloads or failures; insufficient privileges or unsupported OS builds can also interrupt updates. Network unreachable or slow: grab the latest installer from the official download page mirrors (Baidu/Quark/Xunlei cloud drives for China networks — no proxy needed) and run it directly over your existing install; settings and data stay intact. Store builds update via Microsoft Store instead. Stuck on "Extracting files": usually the setup has already completed — verify DeskBox.exe in Task Manager and restart DeskBox to land on the new version. "Insufficient privileges" prompt: right-click the installer and choose "Run as administrator". "System version not supported" prompt: since 1.5.6 the minimum OS is Windows 10 2004 (build 19041); update Windows first. The 1.5.9+ updater checks once a day, backs off 2 hours on failure, skips metered networks during "Auto-download updates", and exposes independent "Show update notifications" and "Show release notes after update" toggles under Settings → About → App updates. A pre-update restore point protects your existing version whenever an install fails or is interrupted. The update fails or won't update — what should I do? Download the latest installer directly from the download page (or its cloud-drive mirrors) and install over your existing build; Store users update via Microsoft Store. The download is really slow — do I need a proxy? Not necessarily — use the cloud-drive mirrors linked on the download page and run the installer directly. It's been stuck on "Extracting" forever. Usually installation already finished. Check Task Manager for DeskBox and restart the app. The update says I don't have enough privileges. Right-click the installer and pick "Run as administrator". Installation says my system version isn't supported. Bring Windows 10 up to at least version 2004 (build 19041) via Windows Update first.

title: What to do about freezes and crashes
summary: Click/drag freezes and todo color-change crashes have largely been resolved in 1.5.9 and 1.6.0. Update to the latest version first; if a fre
faqs: One click on a widget and everything freezes — the desktop stops responding.
Changing a todo's color crashes the app.
DeskBox froze and I can't click anything on the desktop. What now?
Error R6016, "not enough space for thread data".
How do I capture a crash dump (LocalDumps) for debugging?
text: Click/drag freezes and todo color-change crashes have largely been resolved in 1.5.9 and 1.6.0. Update to the latest version first; if a freeze or crash still happens, recover your desktop and capture diagnostic evidence with the steps below. Try Esc first: occasionally a confirmation/transient overlay sits off-focus and blocks input like a modal freeze — pressing Esc (or Enter) dismisses it immediately. Otherwise, recover via Task Manager. Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager. (Optional if frozen and you want to help diagnose: right-click DeskBox.exe and click "Create dump file", noting the .dmp path before ending the task.) End DeskBox processes (including --settings, --studio companions, or background entries), then launch DeskBox again cleanly; your files stay safe on disk. Capturing Windows crash dumps (WER LocalDumps): the official repo guide (docs/support/crash-dumps.md) provides Enable-DeskBoxLocalDumps.ps1 / Disable-DeskBoxLocalDumps.ps1. It edits only HKCU for DeskBox.exe (default MiniDump, or Full on request) and saves dumps locally to %LOCALAPPDATA%\DeskBox\CrashDumps — never auto-uploaded. Run Disable and delete old dumps once troubleshooting finishes. If reproducible, export a privacy-filtered diagnostics bundle from Settings → About → Troubleshooting & diagnostics → "Export diagnostics", and attach it via Settings → About → Feedback → "Send feedback" (which supports multi-turn follow-ups in "My feedback") or GitHub Issues. If DeskBox.ThumbnailProxy.exe reports "not enough space for thread data" (R6016), TLS slots were exhausted by third-party injected DLLs in the system environment — attach your diagnostics bundle so we can help identify the injector. Automatic snapshots protect settings on schedule; export a manual ZIP backup under Settings → Data & backup before major changes. One click on a widget and everything freezes — the desktop stops responding. Try Esc once in case an invisible modal has focus; otherwise end DeskBox in Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) and update to 1.6.0. If reproducible, attach a diagnostics bundle. Changing a todo's color crashes the app. Fixed in 1.5.9+ — please update to the latest build. DeskBox froze and I can't click anything on the desktop. What now? Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc), end DeskBox processes to unfreeze the desktop, then relaunch DeskBox. Error R6016, "not enough space for thread data". System thread-local storage was exhausted by third-party injected DLLs — attach a diagnostics bundle so the conflicting hook can be identified. How do I capture a crash dump (LocalDumps) for debugging? For freezes, right-click DeskBox.exe in Task Manager → "Create dump file". For crashes, run Enable-DeskBoxLocalDumps.ps1 from docs/support/crash-dumps.md (HKCU only, writes to %LOCALAPPDATA%\DeskBox\CrashDumps, never auto-uploaded); disable and delete manually when done.

title: Is high memory or CPU usage normal?
summary: DeskBox lives on the desktop, so resource usage scales with widget count, continuous animations, dynamic live wallpapers (such as Wallpaper
faqs: Is the high memory usage normal?
CPU or GPU stays high (especially with Wallpaper Engine running) — what helps?
How do I minimize idle memory and disk usage?
Why are there extra DeskBox.exe processes in Task Manager, or does anything stay after quitting?
Do animations like vinyl rotation and title marquee cost resources?
Where do I clear image caches in Quick Capture or Glance?
text: DeskBox lives on the desktop, so resource usage scales with widget count, continuous animations, dynamic live wallpapers (such as Wallpaper Engine), and UI caching. Start with Performance mode presets and trim continuous effects if usage looks elevated. Performance mode offers "Best experience / Balanced / Resource saver / Custom" presets; expand to tune "Keep UI cache while hidden" (turn off to release widget UI cache when hidden), "Cache capacity", "Idle cache cleanup", and "Compress memory when idle" (hints Windows to trim physical pages after widgets sit hidden and idle). Sustained CPU mostly comes from continuous decorative effects: toggle off Title marquee, Vinyl rotation, Glance photo rotation, or Capsule ambient glow individually to cut animation wakeups close to zero. Why are there multiple DeskBox.exe processes in Task Manager? In 1.6.0, Settings (DeskBox.exe --settings) and Widget Studio (DeskBox.exe --studio) run in short-lived companion processes alongside DeskBox.ThumbnailProxy.exe. As soon as you close Settings or Studio, its companion exits and reclaims 100% of its UI memory, keeping the resident desktop host lean. Running Wallpaper Engine alongside DeskBox? Mica and Acrylic translucent composition layers on top of animated desktop video add DWM GPU overhead — switch DeskBox material to "Solid", disable "Continuous decorative effects", and pick the "Resource saver" preset for smooth playback. You can also reclaim cached image disk space anytime via Settings → Feature widgets → Quick Capture → Data management (Image cache) and Glance → Image cache. Brief exit wind-down is normal and ends cleanly from Tray → Exit; if usage stays abnormal, export diagnostics from Settings → About → Troubleshooting & diagnostics. Is the high memory usage normal? It reflects widget count and caching settings. Switch Settings → General → Performance & resources to "Resource saver", turn off "Keep UI cache while hidden", and enable "Compress memory when idle". CPU or GPU stays high (especially with Wallpaper Engine running) — what helps? Turn off "Continuous decorative effects" (Title marquee, Vinyl rotation, etc.) under Performance & resources and switch backdrop material to "Solid" under Settings → Appearance → Window material and background. How do I minimize idle memory and disk usage? Pick the "Resource saver" preset (lowers cache budget, releases hidden UI cache, enables idle cleanup/trim) and clean unused Quick Capture / Glance image caches. Why are there extra DeskBox.exe processes in Task Manager, or does anything stay after quitting? Settings (--settings) and Widget Studio (--studio) run in short-lived companion processes that exit immediately when closed; quitting from Tray → Exit cleanly terminates all processes. Do animations like vinyl rotation and title marquee cost resources? Continuous animations keep DWM frames active; uncheck unused ones under Continuous decorative effects to drop animation cost to near zero. Where do I clear image caches in Quick Capture or Glance? Under Settings → Feature widgets → Quick Capture → Data management → Image cache and Settings → Feature widgets → Glance → Image cache.

title: Widgets missing or misplaced after restart or monitor changes
summary: Widget layouts are saved per monitor hardware topology — single laptop display, dual monitors, docked workstation, etc. Switching or unplugg
faqs: Widgets are gone after a restart.
I changed monitors or used Remote Desktop and all widget positions shifted.
After unlocking or resuming from sleep, all widgets vanished.
Where did my widgets go after unplugging an external monitor?
DeskBox warns "Virtual display detected", or widgets stack in the corner on virtual screens.
My configuration broke and all widgets are gone. What now?
text: Widget layouts are saved per monitor hardware topology — single laptop display, dual monitors, docked workstation, etc. Switching or unplugging a screen selects its own layout profile, so missing widgets were usually reflowed or assigned to another monitor. Open Settings → Windows & interaction → Displays: review the interactive monitor map and per-screen widget lists, click Identify to flash display numbers, and check "Show new widgets on". Gather widgets fast: use the monitor card's one-click "Move all to this display" action (with Undo banner even after unplugs). Bind layouts reliably: reassign individual items under "Display for each widget", or right-click a widget / group → "Move to display" so positions track hardware identity across reconnects. Configure "Display connection and scaling behavior": choose "When screen size or scale changes" (keep fixed vs proportional scale), "When a display is disconnected" (reflow or collapse to capsules until reconnected), and "Recalibrate layout". Virtual display adapter warning (1.6.0): if you run Parsec, Sunshine, IDD, or headless virtual displays as your primary monitor, certain GPU drivers can cause corner stacking, flicker, or freezes. If DeskBox displays the virtual-display warning banner, set a physical monitor as your primary Windows display. Resolution or DPI scaling adjustments trigger elastic safety clamping under "When screen size or scale changes" so widgets never drift off-screen. Temporary disappearance after wake from sleep or unlock is normal while topologies reconnect; click "Recalibrate layout" under Displays if anything looks off after wake. Corrupted configuration recovery: since 1.5.9, if configuration is wiped while a snapshot exists, DeskBox prompts once at startup to "Restore from backup / Start fresh". The startup "Restore from backup" prompt appears once — if missed, open Settings → Data & backup to restore manually. Widgets are gone after a restart. Layouts follow monitor combinations. Inspect each display's widget list under Settings → Windows & interaction → Displays and click "Move all to this display" or "Recalibrate layout". I changed monitors or used Remote Desktop and all widget positions shifted. Right-click key widgets → "Move to display" to bind them to a physical monitor, and tune "When screen size or scale changes" under Displays. After unlocking or resuming from sleep, all widgets vanished. Topology reconnects restore widgets shortly after wake; if needed, click "Recalibrate layout" under Settings → Windows & interaction → Displays. Where did my widgets go after unplugging an external monitor? "When a display is disconnected" either reflows widgets onto active screens or collapses them to capsules until you plug that monitor back in. DeskBox warns "Virtual display detected", or widgets stack in the corner on virtual screens. Set a physical monitor as your primary display in Windows Display Settings if using Parsec/Sunshine/virtual adapters, then run "Recalibrate layout" in DeskBox Displays settings. My configuration broke and all widgets are gone. What now? Accept the one-time "Restore from backup" startup prompt, or restore from Automatic/Manual backup under Settings → Data & backup.

title: Material turns black or transparency won't apply
summary: Materials turning black or solid usually mean Windows "Transparency effects" are off, battery saver downgraded effects, or the chosen materi
faqs: How do I make widgets transparent? Where's the transparency setting?
Acrylic turns black — the material isn't applying.
The whole widget is black, or underlying widgets bleed faintly through.
Why can't transparency go all the way — no full transparency?
No Mica effect or simplified motion on Windows 10 / Remote Desktop?
text: Materials turning black or solid usually mean Windows "Transparency effects" are off, battery saver downgraded effects, or the chosen material enforces Windows opacity rules. Open Windows Settings → Personalization → Colors and turn on "Transparency effects" (DeskBox also surfaces a prompt inside Settings → Appearance → Window material and background). Check power mode: on battery saver or unplugged laptops, Windows turns Mica and Acrylic solid; plug in or disable battery saver to restore. Missing transparency slider? "Background transparency" only appears under Lightweight Acrylic, Standard Acrylic, and Solid — Mica hides the slider automatically. Want 100% transparent: select "Solid" material and slide "Background transparency" all the way down (adjust "Text and icon color" under Display density to suit your wallpaper). Windows enforces a minimum visibility floor on Mica and Acrylic materials; only the "Solid" material goes fully transparent. On Windows 10, Remote Desktop (RDP), Hyper-V, or WARP software rendering, 1.6.0 applies compatible downgrades and adaptive motion simplification while keeping frosted visuals intact on physical GPUs. Faintly seeing desktop icons, adjacent widgets, or overlapped boundaries through a translucent widget is normal DWM compositing; search "transparency" in Settings (Ctrl+F) to jump straight to the card. How do I make widgets transparent? Where's the transparency setting? Settings → Appearance → Window material and background → Background transparency. Switch away from Mica to Lightweight Acrylic, Standard Acrylic, or Solid (Solid reaches 100% transparent). Acrylic turns black — the material isn't applying. Enable Windows Settings → Personalization → Colors → "Transparency effects" and verify Battery Saver isn't forcing solid fallback. The whole widget is black, or underlying widgets bleed faintly through. Solid black traces to Transparency effects or power saving; faint background shapes showing through a semi-transparent widget are normal Windows transparency behavior. Why can't transparency go all the way — no full transparency? Windows limits Mica and Acrylic minimum opacity; choose "Solid" with "Background transparency" at minimum to remove the background completely. No Mica effect or simplified motion on Windows 10 / Remote Desktop? Windows 10 downgrades unsupported Mica effects automatically, and 1.6.0 simplifies heavy frosted motion under Win10 / RDP / Hyper-V for smooth performance.

title: Administrator rights: elevation notices and drag limits
summary: Seeing "Administrator privileges detected" or limited cross-window interaction happens when DeskBox, the shortcut launching it, or Windows E
faqs: Why does it keep saying "Administrator privileges detected" when I didn't run as admin?
Icons won't drag and files won't drag out while running as administrator.
I disabled UAC and the administrator notice keeps popping up.
Can I use DeskBox on the built-in Administrator account?
How do I send files to WeChat while elevated, or fix an elevated Explorer?
text: Seeing "Administrator privileges detected" or limited cross-window interaction happens when DeskBox, the shortcut launching it, or Windows Explorer runs elevated. In 1.6.0, Settings → About → Troubleshooting & diagnostics → "Drag-and-drop check" diagnoses all five privilege conditions cleanly. Why is it elevated when I didn't click Run as administrator? Check three hidden causes: (1) .lnk shortcut properties having "Run as administrator" checked (Properties → Shortcut → Advanced → Run as administrator); (2) EXE Compatibility flags forcing RUNASADMIN or Windows 8 compatibility mode (WIN8RTM, which breaks startup/OS version checks); or (3) launching from an elevated terminal, or conversely Windows Explorer itself running elevated (ShellAboveApp) blocking tray activation and standard drops. Click "Restart with standard privileges" in the tray notice or "Drag-and-drop check" to restart unelevated. Open DeskBox shortcut or .exe Properties and uncheck Shortcut → Advanced → Run as administrator and Compatibility overrides (RUNASADMIN / WIN8RTM), then restart. If the entire login session is elevated (UAC disabled or built-in Administrator), review the policy steps below. Since 1.6.0, outbound dragging from elevated widgets to Desktop and File Explorer works via cursor tracking, and dropping onto third-party apps (such as WeChat) copies items so Ctrl+V pastes immediately. With UAC off or on the built-in Administrator account, every process is elevated so "Restart with standard privileges" cannot drop tokens — follow the notice's three options: secpol.msc (Admin Approval Mode), FilterAdministratorToken registry key, or a standard account. Keep Explorer and DeskBox at matching standard privileges day to day; elevate temporarily only when launching admin tools via right-click → Run as administrator or checking Public Desktop during Organize Desktop. Why does it keep saying "Administrator privileges detected" when I didn't run as admin? Open Settings → About → Troubleshooting & diagnostics → "Drag-and-drop check" and inspect .lnk Shortcut → Advanced → Run as administrator, EXE Compatibility (RUNASADMIN / WIN8RTM), or an elevated parent shell. Icons won't drag and files won't drag out while running as administrator. Since 1.6.0, dragging out from widgets to Desktop/Explorer works via pointer tracking and drops to WeChat copy for Ctrl+V, but full cross-window dragging still needs "Restart with standard privileges" (plus Manual sort). I disabled UAC and the administrator notice keeps popping up. Without UAC, the entire session is elevated; follow secpol.msc, FilterAdministratorToken, or switch to a standard user account. Can I use DeskBox on the built-in Administrator account? Yes, though full elevation limits some Windows cross-window drags unless you enable Admin Approval Mode or use a standard account. How do I send files to WeChat while elevated, or fix an elevated Explorer? Drag directly into WeChat and press Ctrl+V; if "Drag-and-drop check" flags ShellAboveApp (Explorer elevated above DeskBox), restart Explorer cleanly as a standard process.

title: Does DeskBox replace the Windows desktop?
summary: No. Windows Explorer remains the desktop shell; DeskBox only adds independently managed widgets above the native desktop without forcefully
faqs: Will the desktop break after uninstalling DeskBox?
Are files placed in widgets still my original files?
Does it affect my wallpaper or context menus?
Why don't DeskBox widgets push native desktop icons out of the way?
text: No. Windows Explorer remains the desktop shell; DeskBox only adds independently managed widgets above the native desktop without forcefully moving or rearranging native desktop icons. Will the desktop break after uninstalling DeskBox? No. Explorer remains the desktop shell throughout — DeskBox only layered widgets on top; after uninstalling, the desktop returns to normal and files are untouched. Are files placed in widgets still my original files? Yes. They stay ordinary files on disk, visible in Explorer too; DeskBox never takes over Explorer. Does it affect my wallpaper or context menus? No. The desktop shell isn't replaced, so your wallpaper and system settings stay as they are; widget context menus only apply to the widgets themselves. Why don't DeskBox widgets push native desktop icons out of the way? DeskBox intentionally never rearranges native Windows desktop icon layout data. Move messy desktop icons into file widgets (or run Organize Desktop), or right-click the Windows desktop → View → uncheck Show desktop icons if you prefer managing everything in DeskBox.

title: How do I report a problem or suggest something?
summary: You can submit feedback without signing up inside the app or on the website: open Settings → About → Feedback → "Send feedback" to report a
faqs: How do I track my feedback and add follow-ups?
What should I attach to a report?
Do feature suggestions count as feedback?
text: You can submit feedback without signing up inside the app or on the website: open Settings → About → Feedback → "Send feedback" to report a bug (with an optional privacy-filtered diagnostics bundle) or suggest a feature. Starting in 1.6.0, "My feedback" lets you read official replies and post multi-turn follow-ups directly inside the app. You can also browse progress, upvote, or reply on the public feedback community at deskbox.fun/feedback, or open a GitHub Issue. Chinese users can also leave feedback on the WeChat account "Dayu Lab (大雨实验室)". How do I track my feedback and add follow-ups? In-app feedback gets a feedback ID: check status, read official replies, and send multi-turn follow-ups under Settings → About → Feedback → "My feedback", or follow publicly on deskbox.fun/feedback with no account required. What should I attach to a report? Export a diagnostics bundle (privacy-filtered) from Settings → About → Troubleshooting & diagnostics, attach it, and describe the steps to reproduce; in-app bug reports can attach and upload it automatically. Do feature suggestions count as feedback? Yes. Both in-app feedback and the feedback community accept problems and suggestions — many features started as user feedback.

title: Compatibility and known limitations
summary: DeskBox installs and runs on most Windows 10/11 PCs, but a few system and third-party environments impose limits: game anti-cheat, antivirus
faqs: I get a "system environment error" playing League of Legends (WeGame). Is it DeskBox?
My antivirus says DeskBox is a trojan. Where is safe to download?
My third-party IME (e.g. Sogou) won't type in search/notes, or IME toggles on reveal.
Shortcuts remain in a widget after uninstalling, or reappear after updating an app.
The music widget's progress bar doesn't show or won't drag. Why?
Does the Microsoft Store version have any functional limits vs Direct?
text: DeskBox installs and runs on most Windows 10/11 PCs, but a few system and third-party environments impose limits: game anti-cheat, antivirus false positives, third-party IME quirks, and more. Here is what to expect and how to handle each. Game anti-cheat: some games' anti-cheat software blocks desktop organizers. Riot Vanguard may terminate DeskBox while running (disabling global hotkeys can help); Tencent ACE combined with a local proxy may trigger a "system environment error". Exit DeskBox or disable proxies/use Desktop pinned layer before launching those games. Antivirus false positives & fake downloads: official Direct installers are currently unsigned and may trigger false positives. Verify code or check .sha256 hashes, and download only from deskbox.fun, GitHub Releases, or Microsoft Store — never use search-ad or third-party "high-speed downloader" wrappers. Third-party IME quirks: occasionally third-party IMEs (e.g. Sogou) fail to commit text inside WinUI 3 inputs (Global Search, Quick Capture, Settings) — switch to Windows' built-in Microsoft IME as a reliable workaround. Brief EN/CN switching on widget reveal reflects current Windows keyboard focus switching. Leftover & returning desktop shortcuts: third-party uninstallers don't clear shortcuts moved into widgets (delete manually), and app updates may recreate icons on the shared Windows Public Desktop, which auto-organize leaves untouched for safety (run Organize Desktop manually with Public Desktop checked when needed). Microsoft Store MSIX sandbox: core desktop organization and 6 built-in widgets match Direct, except Store disables Custom Widget Local Command Execution and treats AppData paths as read-only. Music progress bar: playback position comes from the media player via Windows SMTC, and players that omit position won't show a draggable seek bar (see "Music widget won't detect NetEase Cloud Music or QQ Music?"). Windows 10 & virtual displays: Mica degrades on Win10, and 1.6.0 simplifies heavy acrylic motion under Win10 / RDP / Hyper-V; avoid setting virtual display adapters as primary if corner stacking occurs. Memory & GPU tuning: keep performance snappy alongside live wallpapers (like Wallpaper Engine) by choosing Solid material, turning off continuous decorative effects, and selecting the Resource saver preset. The interface supports 13 languages. Hit a compatibility edge case? Attach a diagnostics bundle from Settings → About → Troubleshooting & diagnostics to your feedback. I get a "system environment error" playing League of Legends (WeGame). Is it DeskBox? It can be anti-cheat related: Tencent ACE with a local proxy may trigger a system environment error — exit DeskBox or disable the proxy before playing; Riot Vanguard may also stop DeskBox while active (try Desktop pinned layer or toggling off global hotkeys). My antivirus says DeskBox is a trojan. Where is safe to download? Unsigned binaries can cause false positives. Download strictly from deskbox.fun, GitHub Releases, or Microsoft Store (never search-ad downloader bundles), and verify against .sha256 before running. My third-party IME (e.g. Sogou) won't type in search/notes, or IME toggles on reveal. Some third-party IMEs misbehave in WinUI 3 text inputs — switching to the built-in Windows IME resolves it; transient language switches on widget reveal are normal focus behavior. Shortcuts remain in a widget after uninstalling, or reappear after updating an app. Third-party uninstallers don't clean shortcuts inside widgets (delete manually), and app updates often write fresh icons to the shared Public Desktop (sort manually in Organize Desktop). The music widget's progress bar doesn't show or won't drag. Why? Playback progress is reported by the player over Windows SMTC — some players do not expose position or seek. Does the Microsoft Store version have any functional limits vs Direct? Only two MSIX boundaries: Custom Widget Local Command Execution is disabled and AppData directories are read-only — everything else matches Direct.
